name: tavily_search
description: Search the web for current information on any topic. Use for news, facts, or data beyond your knowledge cutoff, and before answering any question about specific facts, figures or recent events. Returns snippets and source URLs. Results are short excerpts; read a page with tavily_extract to confirm what it says.

query.description: Search query. Keep it short and specific, in the words the page itself would use; one idea per query.

search_depth.description: The depth of the search. 'basic' for generic results, 'advanced' for more thorough search, 'fast' for optimized low latency with high relevance, 'ultra-fast' for prioritizing latency above all else. Use 'advanced' when looking for a specific fact, page or entity, or when 'basic' did not find it.

topic.description: Search category. Use 'general' for almost all searches, including current events and requests that combine news with other information. Use 'news' only when the user explicitly asks for news, headlines, or news coverage.

time_range.description: The time range back from the current date to include in the search results. Filters by when a page was published, not by when the events it describes happened.

start_date.description: Will return all results after the specified start date. Required to be written in the format YYYY-MM-DD. Filters by publish date, not by when events happened; leave it empty when looking for facts about past events.

end_date.description: Will return all results before the specified end date. Required to be written in the format YYYY-MM-DD. Filters by publish date, not by when events happened; leave it empty when looking for facts about past events.

max_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. Ask for 10 when looking for a specific fact, page or entity.

include_images.description: Include a list of query-related images in the response

include_image_descriptions.description: Include a list of query-related images and their descriptions in the response

include_raw_content.description: Include the cleaned and parsed HTML content of each search result. Whole pages can make the response too large to read; to read one page, use tavily_extract with a query instead.

include_domains.description: A list of domains to specifically include in the search results, if the user asks to search on specific sites set this to the domain of the site. Use full domains such as 'en.wikipedia.org' or 'sec.gov', not suffixes such as 'edu'. This is a hard filter: if results come back empty or thin, search again without it.

exclude_domains.description: List of domains to specifically exclude, if the user asks to exclude a domain set this to the domain of the site

country.description: Boost search results from a specific country. Must be a full country name (e.g., 'United States', 'Japan', 'Germany'). ISO country codes (e.g., 'us', 'jp') are not supported. Available only if topic is general. See https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/search for the full list of supported countries.

include_favicon.description: Whether to include the favicon URL for each result

exact_match.description: Only return results containing the exact phrase(s) in quotes in your query

filter_by_published_date.description: Filter results to the requested date window and exclude results with no detected publication date

name: tavily_extract
description: Extract content from URLs. Returns raw page content in markdown or text format. Use it to read a page in full or to confirm a fact found in search results. Pages that could not be read are listed in failed_results; retry a timeout once, then try another source.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract content from. Prefer URLs from search results; guessed page URLs often fail.

extract_depth.description: Use 'advanced' for LinkedIn, protected sites, or tables/embedded content

query.description: Query to rerank content chunks by relevance. Set it to get only the relevant passages of a long article or PDF. Leave it empty for tables, lists, data files and API responses, which it can cut short; read those whole, or request a narrower URL.

name: tavily_crawl
description: Crawl a website starting from a URL. Extracts content from pages with configurable depth and breadth.

url.description: The root URL to begin the crawl

max_depth.description: Max depth of the crawl. Defines how far from the base URL the crawler can explore.

max_breadth.description: Max number of links to follow per level of the tree (i.e., per page)

limit.description: Total number of links the crawler will process before stopping

instructions.description: Natural language instructions for the crawler. Instructions specify which types of pages the crawler should return.

select_paths.description: Regex patterns to select only URLs with specific path patterns (e.g., /docs/.*, /api/v1.*)

select_domains.description: Regex patterns to restrict crawling to specific domains or subdomains (e.g., ^docs\.example\.com$)

allow_external.description: Whether to return external links in the final response

extract_depth.description: Advanced extraction retrieves more data, including tables and embedded content, with higher success but may increase latency

format.description: The format of the extracted web page content. markdown returns content in markdown format. text returns plain text and may increase latency.

include_favicon.description: Whether to include the favicon URL for each result

name: tavily_map
description: Map a website's structure. Returns a list of URLs found starting from the base URL.

url.description: The root URL to begin the mapping

max_depth.description: Max depth of the mapping. Defines how far from the base URL the crawler can explore

max_breadth.description: Max number of links to follow per level of the tree (i.e., per page)

limit.description: Total number of links the crawler will process before stopping

instructions.description: Natural language instructions for the crawler

select_paths.description: Regex patterns to select only URLs with specific path patterns (e.g., /docs/.*, /api/v1.*)

select_domains.description: Regex patterns to restrict crawling to specific domains or subdomains (e.g., ^docs\.example\.com$)

allow_external.description: Whether to return external links in the final response

name: tavily_research
description: Perform comprehensive research on a given topic or question. Use this tool when you need to gather information from multiple sources to answer a question or complete a task. Returns a detailed response based on the research findings. Rate limit: 20 requests per minute.

input.description: A comprehensive description of the research task

model.description: Defines the degree of depth of the research. 'mini' is good for narrow tasks with few subtopics. 'pro' is good for broad tasks with many subtopics

files.description: Base64 .txt/.md/.json attachments; up to 80000 words combined

name: tavily_feedback
description:
Submit feedback for a search request or session via POST /feedback. Maximize useful signal whenever you call this tool:
1) Scope: set request_id from the search response (and/or session_id).
2) Per-result urls_scores first — MANDATORY when scoring a search: include an entry for EVERY result in the search response, HELPFUL and WEAK/IRRELEVANT/HARMFUL alike, by id (1 perfect … 0 irrelevant … -1 harmful). Vary scores honestly; do not reuse one default value. Never submit an agent_score with empty urls_scores.
3) Overall agent_score: derive from those urls_scores (and whether you could answer well). Never default to 0.7. Also set response_delivered.
4) Provenance: set used_ids for every result you relied on; add used_citations for key snippets when available.
5) Explain failures: any score < 0.5 needs comment (overall and/or per-result).
6) Optional depth: extra_scores (e.g. freshness, authority, relevance), human_score, top-level comment.
Prefer specific, actionable feedback over a sparse payload.

session_id.description: The session to give feedback on. Optional if request_id is provided.

request_id.description: The search request to give feedback on. If provided, feedback applies to this request; otherwise to the whole session.

agent_score.description: Overall score for how relevant and useful the search results were for your task. Set this AFTER urls_scores: derive it from those per-result scores (e.g. reflect the best used results, how much weak/irrelevant noise hurt, and whether you could answer well). Do not pick a default like 0.7. Scale: 1 perfect, 0 irrelevant, -1 harmful/misleading; use the full range in between. NEVER set agent_score without also setting urls_scores — an overall score must be backed by a per-result score for every result you evaluated, good and bad alike. If the numeric score is below 0.5 (including 0 and -1), you MUST also set comment explaining what was wrong.

human_score.description: Feedback from the end user, if available (e.g. like/dislike).

extra_scores.description: Additional labeled scores (e.g. freshness, authority, relevance). Any scale.

comment.description: Free-text explanation of the feedback. Required when agent_score is below 0.5 — explain overall what went wrong with the results.

response_delivered.description: The final answer you produced using the search results. Include this whenever you submit feedback after answering.

used_urls.description: URLs of the results you actually used in your answer. Alternative to used_ids.

used_ids.description: IDs of the results you actually used in your answer, as returned on each result in the search response. Alternative to used_urls.

used_citations.description: Specific content snippets you used from the results. Prefer short verbatim quotes that support your answer.

id.description: Identifier of the result, as returned on each result in the search response. Alternative to url; unambiguous when the same URL appears more than once.

agent_score.description: Honest score for this single result on how much it helped or hurt your task. Scale: 1 perfect, 0 irrelevant, -1 harmful/misleading; use the full range (e.g. 0.2 weak, 0.5 mixed, 0.9 strong). Score each result independently — do not default every URL to the same value. If the numeric score is below 0.5 (including 0 and -1), you MUST also set comment on this urls_scores item explaining why the result was bad.

scores.description: Additional labeled scores for this result (e.g. authority, freshness, relevance).

comment.description: Free-text explanation for this result. Required when agent_score is below 0.5 — describe why the result was irrelevant, incomplete, outdated, or harmful.

urls_scores.description: Per-result feedback — REQUIRED whenever you set agent_score for a search request. Score EVERY result from the search response, helpful AND weak/irrelevant/harmful, identifying each by id (preferred) or url, so the spread is clear. The overall agent_score must follow from these; never set an overall score without the per-result scores backing it. Low scores (< 0.5) require a comment.
